correctness.rationale: For every real 0<delta,p<1, both skew tent branches have Lebesgue-preserving transfer operators. On Y=x-1/2 and H=Y²-1/12 the verified exact action is P_s Y=s delta Y and P_s H=((1+3delta²)/4)H-((1-delta²)/4)Y. Stationary symmetric Markov signs have consecutive product mean zero for odd length and (2p-1)^(length/2) for even length. Combining these identities proves the complete all-lag anti-reversal cubic series and its rational generating function. A finite geometric series determines every sign; the quadratic discriminant gives the sharp p=1/8 boundary including equality. The independent affine-cylinder rational verifier exactly matched both directional integrals in 40 cases of lag up to eight and passed six phase identities. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove the infinite assertion.

The published 2003 deterministic skew-tent formula covers the fixed-map special case and is expressly excluded from the novelty claim. A 2013 iid random-intermittent analysis and a 2017 Markov-switching *coupling/synchronization* analysis concern different maps and observables, respectively. Direct source and claim-equivalence searches found no exact p=1/8 threshold, four-lag sign pattern or all-lag generating function. This is best-knowledge originality, with the broad moment-theory and access risks recorded; no absolute-priority claim.

value.rationale: Time-direction asymmetry is a natural observable of stationary chaotic dynamics, and Markov-persistent forcing is a natural model of temporally correlated environmental switching. Despite a reversible driving chain and invariant uniform spatial marginals, the observable always detects irreversibility at lag one; the complete two-parameter phase diagram determines when higher lags reverse sign, vanish identically at two mod-four residue classes, or retain one sign. The sharp environmental threshold p=1/8 and competing singularities of the exact generating function are structurally motivated rather than a narrow unmotivated numeric invariant.
